Current release queue, 7 October 2026: release-1.0; milestone-release.
Plan: docs/refactor/RELEASE-QUEUE.md. Mote remains authoritative; one primary agent and at most one helper.

Reconciliation: The historic 422 enum cases are an inventory, not 422 established forgeability defects. Stable-symbol list approval is complete; final stable-boundary construction judgment is not.

Remaining / next action: Audit the approved stable, receipt-reachable public constructors first: prove relational invariants at checked factories or document an honest open boundary. Close stable judgment before API freeze; keep the broader enum census as later maintenance.

Release tags schedule work; they do not establish completion or empirical qualification. Use current AGENTS.md for ownership, scoped gates and exact-SHA review; old fleet roles, timers and fixed gate task counts are historical. Keep the original scientific preregistration, denominators, admission and sealed-test rules below.

Retained acceptance and design context:

Scheduling lane: maintenance. Current plan: docs/refactor/PLAN.md. Live dependency edges supersede historical sequencing below.

Current disposition, 2026-09-19; governing docs/refactor/PLAN.md.
Retained with its original acceptance scope; recheck against current code before implementation or closure. Not a prerequisite for the annotation-assisted preview.

Original scope retained below for evidence; fleet procedure/assignments are historical and do not govern single-developer work.

RAISED BY claude-storymodel4s-m1 after the chief asked them to attack his corrected enumeration pattern. They found it in twenty minutes and it is not another regex flaw.

A PARAMETERISED ENUM CASE IS A CONSTRUCTIBLE PRODUCT TYPE AND NO `case class` PATTERN WILL EVER SEE ONE. Measured on ExclusionCause.BelowMembership from outside its package: Mirror TRUE, apply TRUE, copy TRUE. In Scala 3 an enum case with parameters is a case class in every respect except the two words we grep for.

SIZE OF THE UNSEEN SURFACE, measured by the chief:
  private-constructor case classes (three sweeps' population):   42
  parameterised enum cases in main sources:                     422

NOT 422 DEFECTS. Most are legitimately public data carriers with nothing to protect; counting them as at-risk would be over-claiming. The point is that the set of types whose construction we have never ENUMERATED is an order of magnitude larger than the set we spent three sweeps closing.

ALREADY BIT US ONCE: collab blocked m1's candidate this morning because PlacementResolution.of accepted BelowMembership(NaN), infinities, -0.1 and 1.1 and published each as the rule in force. They found it BY CONSTRUCTING ONE -- through exactly this door. The first instance was found by an independent reviewer and none of us recognised it as a population problem.

THE DEFINITION CHANGES: we want CONSTRUCTIBLE PRODUCT TYPES WITH INVARIANTS. We were enumerating a SYNTACTIC FORM while believing we enumerated a SEMANTIC PROPERTY, and every regex refinement was a better approximation of the wrong target.

TWO LEGITIMATE REMEDIES, chosen per type:
  UNFORGEABLE -- plain final class, private constructor, explicit accessors. Confirmed to defeat Mirror in Scala 3.7.4 at dad96e6.
  WIRE BOUNDARY -- the value can be built but cannot enter a computation; validate at `of` or at every boundary it crosses. m1 chose this for BelowMembership and the chief agrees: an enum case is a vocabulary, and sealing every parameterised case would be absurd.

So the sweep question is NOT 'is it sealed' but 'does an invariant exist, and is it enforced at construction OR at every boundary the value can cross'.

FIRST SLICE IS A JUDGEMENT PASS, NOT A PROBE CAMPAIGN: which parameterised enum cases carry an invariant that construction could violate? Start from those reachable in PUBLISHED RECEIPTS. Expect a much smaller number worth defending. A sweep that treats 'unsealed' as 'defective' will generate hundreds of false findings and discredit the exercise.
